transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-06
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Alice Ramirez (Redwood AE), Ben Cho (Redwood SE), Maria Gonzalez (CTO, SummitCare), Tom Baker (Lead Platform Engineer), Nina Patel (Security)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough focused on org/project keys, rate limits and quotas, and multi-tenant controls. Customer has questions about scoping API keys to projects, per-route quotas, tenant isolation (hosted vs dedicated), encryption/KMS and audit logs. Agreed next steps: share pricing + security docs, pilot with dedicated test project, schedule deeper technical session.

Topics:
- Org vs project keys and scoping
- Per-route and global rate limits, burst and steady-state policies
- Dedicated vs hosted capacity for predictable latency
- RBAC, SSO, KMS/HSM and audit logs
- Monitoring and token-level cost breakdowns in Console

Transcript:
[00:00] Alice Ramirez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alice with Redwood, and with me is Ben, our solutions engineer. Maria: hi.
[00:14] Maria Gonzalez: Hi Alice, thanks. We wanted to focus this session on rate limiting and how we can isolate tenants — we run a multi-tenant clinician portal and need per-organization quotas.
[00:30] Ben Cho: Great, yeah we'll show the console and API. quick note, some names might come out weird on the transcript, but I'll try to be clear.
[00:45] Tom Baker: timeline — we're looking at a Q3 pilot, but we need to lock down security and the way keys are scoped first. Also we have some on-prem constraints on PHI.
[01:02] Nina Patel: And also SOC two compliance and KMS — we need to know how keys are rotated and where logs are stored.
[01:20] Alice Ramirez: Totally. high level, Redwood supports org-level and project-level API keys. you create an org, then projects under it. org keys can span projects, project keys are scoped. we'll demo per-route quotas and token-based budgeting in the console.
[01:40] Ben Cho: jumping into the console — (screen share sounds) — here's the org dashboard, you can see Projects on the left. I'll open SummitCare-Test project.
[02:00] Ben Cho: under Settings -> Keys, you can create keys and set scopes. For example: read-only, generation, embeddings. Keys can be restricted to specific routes and to IP ranges.
[02:20] Maria Gonzalez: can we limit a key to "generation:chat" only, not embeddings?
[02:28] Ben Cho: yes, you can scope by capability; in the API it's an attribute on the key. (mumbles) sometimes called route-scoped keys or project tokens.
[02:45] Tom Baker: and rotation? we need automated rotation via KMS/HSM.
[02:52] Ben Cho: rotation is supported — Redwood integrates with customer KMS for key wrap; we can also rotate keys in the console and support automatic expiry. I'll share our KMS integration doc.
[03:10] Alice Ramirez: On rate limits: you can define global quotas at the org-level and more granular quotas per project or per-route. there are steady-state qps and burst tokens — think of it like token bucket.
[03:30] Ben Cho: here's the Rate Limits page — you can set requests per minute, tokens per minute, and a separate burst window. you can also create policies by customer tier — e.g., free tier: 5 rps, enterprise: 200 rps.
[03:50] Maria Gonzalez: how do we enforce per-customer quotas inside a single project if they all call the same project key?
[03:58] Ben Cho: two options: use project-scoped keys per customer (recommended), or use your own internal identity header and send sub-tenant id — Redwood offers per-tenant metering with our routing rules and you can map headers to quota buckets. the former is simpler for multi-tenant SaaS.
[04:20] Tom Baker: so best practice is one project per product area, and keys per-tenant?
[04:25] Alice Ramirez: yes, or you can have a single project and create many project-keys for tenant isolation; Projects are light-weight.
[04:40] Nina Patel: audit logs — what gets recorded? request headers, ip, model used?
[04:47] Ben Cho: audit logs include call metadata, key id, timestamps, model id, and response codes. payloads with PHI are excluded by default in hosted mode unless you opt-in to retention. for Private deployments we can keep full logs in your VPC.
[05:05] Maria Gonzalez: what's the difference between hosted and dedicated in terms of isolation?
[05:12] Alice Ramirez: hosted — logical isolation, with strong tenant scoping; Dedicated — physical isolation, you get reserved GPU pools, dedicated tenancy and SLA. Dedicated also gives network isolation options and private control plane.
[05:30] Tom Baker: latency is our SLO: p95 < 200ms for short completions. Does dedicated guarantee that?
[05:38] Ben Cho: Dedicated allows more deterministic performance due to reserved capacity; we publish performance profiles per model and can run a benchmark with your traffic to validate. we'll include recommended instance types and quantization profiles.
[05:58] Maria Gonzalez: pricing — how do quotas translate to cost?
[06:05] Alice Ramirez: Console shows token-level cost breakdowns per route and per key. you can set budget alerts and hard quotas that block requests when exceeded, or soft quotas that throttle.
[06:20] Ben Cho: demo: creating a rate-limit policy now — (clicks) — name: "Clinician-Default" — steady: 1200 tokens/min, burst: 500 tokens/30s, per-key enforcement.
[06:45] Alice Ramirez: note that tokens here are model tokens; we surface estimates, and you can map token budgets to dollar budgets.
[07:00] Tom Baker: what about retries from clients? we have a lot of short retries that spike.
[07:06] Ben Cho: You can set backoff-window rules and a retry budget — Redwood's gateway will return standard 429 with Retry-After and you can configure a grace-burst for transient spikes.
[07:25] Maria Gonzalez: can we route traffic to a cheaper model when limits hit?
[07:31] Ben Cho: yes, routing policies allow fallback to a lower-cost model variant or to a slower but cheaper queue. that's built into the smart routing and rollout features.
[07:45] Alice Ramirez: also you can set per-route fallback policies so critical routes have conservative throttling and fallback to noop or cached responses.
[07:58] Tom Baker: about RBAC: can we limit who in our org can create keys?
[08:04] Ben Cho: yes, RBAC integrates with SSO (SAML/Okta). roles: Org Admin, Billing, Project Admin, Read-Only. you can block key creation to only project admins.
[08:20] Nina Patel: SSO provisioning? SCIM?
[08:23] Ben Cho: Yup we support SCIM provisioning for Okta and most IdPs.
[08:30] Maria Gonzalez: data residency — all our data must stay in EU.
[08:34] Alice Ramirez: We have regional hosting and Private deployments; for strict residency we recommend Private in your region or Dedicated with region pinned.
[08:48] Tom Baker: demoing alerts — (screen) — alerts are tied to projects and keys, you can set thresholds and webhooks.
[09:05] Ben Cho: we'll also export metrics to your Prometheus or Datadog: per-route tokens, latency, error rates, cost.
[09:20] Maria Gonzalez: ok this is helpful. can you show how per-project keys look in API calls?
[09:26] Ben Cho: example curl: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer proj-key-abc" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha","input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
[09:40] Ben Cho: the header contains the key id and the gateway maps it to project quotas and rate limits.
[09:50] Tom Baker: we use Kong as our gateway; can Redwood integrate?
[09:55] Ben Cho: we have a sidecar pattern and standard HTTP integration. you can front Redwood with Kong or envoy; or call our API gateway directly.
[10:10] Maria Gonzalez: what's the behavior when a key is revoked mid-flight?
[10:16] Ben Cho: revocation takes effect at the gateway for new requests; in-flight calls may finish depending on lifecycle. there is an option for immediate kill in Dedicated/Private.
[10:30] Alice Ramirez: I want to show the policy UI for org-level quotas. (click) here's org policy "Enterprise Tier" — applied to all projects tagged with enterprise. you can add project tags to apply policies.
[10:50] Ben Cho: tags are powerful for multi-product orgs — tag projects by customer, environment, or team.
[11:05] Maria Gonzalez: what's the request id format, for correlation with our logs?
[11:10] Ben Cho: every request has a trace id we emit in response headers x-rd-trace-id, and we include that in audit logs exported to S3 or your logging endpoint.
[11:25] Tom Baker: can we get raw request/response logs for debug in a dev pilot?
[11:31] Ben Cho: Yes, for pilots we can enable higher-fidelity logging in a demo project; for production you'd want to manage retention and privacy.
[11:45] Maria Gonzalez: how do we do tenant-aware billing? we need cost by customer for chargeback.
[11:52] Alice Ramirez: Console gives per-key and per-route spend breakdown, exportable to CSV. you can also tag requests for internal chargeback keys.
[12:10] Ben Cho: showing billing export — here's per-project token spend by day. you can filter by key.
[12:25] Tom Baker: If we use project-per-tenant, will the number of keys scale? we have thousands of clinics.
[12:33] Ben Cho: Projects and keys are lightweight; we also support API to programmatically create keys and rotate them. we recommend grouping low-volume tenants under a shared key if that fits your billing model.
[12:50] Maria Gonzalez: any rate limiting at the per-IP level?
[12:55] Ben Cho: yes IP restrictions are supported and you can combine IP + key + header for layered enforcement.
[13:10] Nina Patel: encryption in transit and at rest?
[13:13] Alice Ramirez: TLS everywhere in hosted and private; at rest encryption via customer-managed KMS in Private/Dedicated.
[13:25] Tom Baker: ok let's talk failure modes: what happens during region outage?
[13:30] Ben Cho: smart routing can failover to another region if you allow cross-region data flow; otherwise Dedicated private deployments support multi-az within the region.
[13:46] Maria Gonzalez: do you have SOC two and ISO docs?
[13:50] Alice Ramirez: yes, we'll share SOC 2 and ISO attestation and our architecture diagram. Ben will send the security pack after the call.
[14:05] Ben Cho: demo: create a per-route quota — route /v1/generate/chat set to 50 requests/min for staging. I'll show the block behavior, sending a 429. (sends test) you can see Request 47/50 then 50/50 then 429.
[14:35] Tom Baker: nice. any burst exceptions?
[14:39] Ben Cho: we set a burst allowance — you can allow a temporary extra 20 requests over a 30s window.
[14:55] Maria Gonzalez: can the console generate API calls for infra to automate creation?
[15:02] Ben Cho: yes every action in the UI has an equivalent API endpoint — we have full API docs and a Terraform provider in beta.
[15:20] Tom Baker: we use Terraform heavily, that'd be ideal.
[15:25] Maria Gonzalez: show us an example of a fallback policy when a quota is exceeded.
[15:30] Ben Cho: here — fallback to model: redwood-lite with lower token limits, or to cached response. I'll simulate. (sim) request hits, then switches to fallback.
[15:50] Nina Patel: for compliance we need to know where keys are stored — are raw keys stored in your DB?
[15:56] Ben Cho: keys are stored encrypted, we don't store plaintext; for customer-managed KMS the key material is in your KMS and we store only wrapped keys.
[16:12] Tom Baker: do you support per-organization SSO enforced for console? we don't want shared logins.
[16:18] Alice Ramirez: yes SAML enforced org-wide and you can require 2FA from the IdP.
[16:30] Maria Gonzalez: what about monitoring — can we alert when token spend exceeds threshold?
[16:36] Ben Cho: yes, budget alerts and webhooks. we can also push metrics to Datadog if you want.
[16:48] Tom Baker: about private deployment — what's involved to stand up a private control plane?
[16:54] Alice Ramirez: we provide an installer and a config repo; typical timeline 4–8 weeks for Private with integration tests. For Dedicated it's faster, 2–4 weeks depending on cloud region and capacity.
[17:12] Maria Gonzalez: do you support HSM for key operations?
[17:16] Ben Cho: yes, HSM via supported KMS providers for Private/Dedicated.
[17:25] Tom Baker: can we run a short benchmark now or later? we can share sample traces.
[17:30] Ben Cho: we'll run an initial benchmark in the pilot; please send sample traffic patterns.
[17:38] Alice Ramirez: ok quick recap — we'll send pricing + security docs, Ben will send the KMS/HSM guide and RBAC examples, and Tom will send traffic patterns.
[17:50] Maria Gonzalez: sounds good. budget question: how do you price dedicated capacity?
[17:55] Alice Ramirez: reserved capacity is monthly, based on committed GPU hours and instance types, with burst overage pricing. we'll include a sample worksheet in the follow-up.
[18:10] Ben Cho: one more note: we can enforce hard quotas that return 403 or 429, or soft quotas that throttle. choose per-route.
[18:25] Tom Baker: any gotchas when using project keys at scale?
[18:29] Ben Cho: watch for key explosion if you use one key per tiny tenant; automate lifecycle and rotation. use tags and group policies to manage at scale.
[18:45] Maria Gonzalez: okay thanks, that was super helpful.
[18:50] Alice Ramirez: thanks all. We'll send follow-ups.
[18:55] (end of main demo)
